book_paragraphs: GraniteShares 2x Long NBIS Daily ETF is rated REJECTED at Tier Zero for new capital, and our active portfolio instruction is EXIT_IMMEDIATELY on all fifty shares held in the Robinhood account. On Friday, November 20, 2026, NBIL collapsed thirty-two point four-five percent to two dollars and twenty-nine cents, slicing cleanly through our locked two-dollar-and-ninety-two-cent structural stop and locking in a ninety-six point six-six percent drawdown from its fifty-two-week high.

This ten-chapter refresh strips away prior price anchors to examine both layers of the instrument from primary SEC filings. First, inside the wrapper itself, GraniteShares' audited N-CSR and October 2026 summary prospectus expose a one-point-four-one percent net expense ratio, a one-point-four-five percent indirect swap cost, and a single-counterparty Clear Street swap charging OBFR01 plus six hundred basis points. Meanwhile, assets under management shrank sixty-eight percent to sixty-two point two-six million dollars behind lower-cost multi-dealer rivals NEBX and NBIG, just as GraniteShares moved to liquidate twelve sub-scale YieldBOOST funds.

Second, inside the underlying enterprise, Nebius Group's third-quarter 2026 footnotes reveal immense senior claims and accounting caveats behind its ninety-eighty-million-dollar quarterly revenue headline. Three customers accounted for seventy percent of revenue, two customers held eighty-five percent of four billion dollars in receivables, and management extended server depreciation from four years to five years while taking on sixteen point five-nine billion dollars of uncommenced lease and power commitments.

Running those audited inputs through the discrete two-times Geometric Brownian Motion compounding equation yields a twelve-month base target of one dollar and two cents and a probability-weighted expected value of one dollar and twenty-three cents—nearly forty-seven percent below Friday's close. Liquidating all fifty shares at or near two dollars and twenty-nine cents recovers one hundred fourteen dollars and fifty cents into Treasury bill cash while harvesting a taxable loss and cleaning a misclassified leveraged position off the books.

Why this structural asymmetry matters for ordinary portfolio capital becomes clearest when we strip away AI cloud narratives and isolate the arithmetic of daily leverage compounding. A two-times daily ETF does not merely amplify the twelve-month destination of Nebius Group common shares. Instead, it resets notional exposure at the closing bell every trading session in New York. When underlying shares oscillate wildly around a sideways or downward trend, every rebound applies double leverage to a shrunken principal base, while every pullback trims gains before the next advance begins.

At NBIL, this mathematical tax collides head-on with three layers of direct wrapper friction documented across GraniteShares public filings: a net annual operating expense ratio of 1.41 percent, estimated indirect swap expenses of 1.45 percent in FY2027, and an unhedged OBFR01 plus 600 basis points swap financing spread paid to Clear Street as sole counterparty. Combined with volatile data-center buildout schedules, rising lease commitments, and a confirmed Stage 4 breakdown across weekly, daily, and intraday charts, capital preservation leaves no room for hesitation.
